content.text:
Let me analyze this carefully.

The ticket: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: Two notes about employee E039.

Note 1 (HR): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation Payroll: write. Comment: full-time Analyst. Requested admin, role doesn't own Payroll, so admin not permitted. Granting write.

Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation Payroll: read. Comment: contractor with basic security training. Contractors can never have admin; write requires advanced training. Requested admin, so granting max allowed: read. Also notes that Security record is authoritative (earlier note listed full_time, but Security record is authoritative).

So there's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor and is authoritative.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write; admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist). So max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → read.

The Security note claims authority and says contractor with basic training → read.

So the correct decision: requested admin is above max (read), so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
